measurement: where the cost of one rung-2 Lean verification actually goes

conditions.mathlib_floor_only: a file containing only `import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring` and one trivial theorem -- the irreducible per-invocation cost
conditions.spec_alone: the frozen spec compiled by itself
conditions.audit_file_inlined: what verify_against_spec does today: spec body inlined, plus candidate, plus named obligations
conditions.candidate_imports_spec: spec built once as an olean (77.9 s, 734 jobs) and imported instead of inlined

conclusion: Essentially the entire cost is loading Mathlib.Tactic.Ring. The bare import floor (median 17.61 s) is the SLOWEST of the four conditions -- higher than the full audit file (16.49 s) and the spec alone (12.55 s). All four medians lie in a 1.40x band while same-input spreads reach 2.60x, so they are indistinguishable on this host. The spec body, the candidate and the obligations contribute nothing measurable.
a_correction_to_my_own_claim: I previously reported that the frozen spec is ~76% of a verification's cost, inferred from spec-alone (12.55 s) against the audit file (16.49 s). That was wrong: spec-alone ALSO pays the Mathlib import, so the figure attributed a shared fixed cost to the spec. Measuring the import floor separately is what exposed it.
consequences: No per-candidate saving is available from caching a verdict, modularising a genome, or importing the spec instead of inlining it. Building the spec as an olean cost 77.9 s and bought a 1.14x median change, which is inside the noise.
This retroactively explains why all three life-inspired proposals' savings were illusory: every one of them optimised something that is not the cost.

The only lever the measurement supports is amortising the Mathlib load across many candidates in ONE process -- a persistent Lean process or server verifying candidates in sequence -- which is a process-architecture change with no evolutionary or biological content whatsoever.
not_established: n=5 per condition. These are medians with large spreads, adequate to show the conditions are indistinguishable but not to characterise any distribution.
Process reuse was NOT built or measured; its saving is predicted by the decomposition, not demonstrated.
A spec with heavier proofs than 7 ring-closable theorems could shift the balance; this result is for this spec.
